correctness.rationale: The exact border-length reduction and circular centered-height identity are proved. Exhaustive loops enumerate all 2^n binary strings for each n=1..16, reject exactly the nonprimitive powers, test all cyclic roots and k up to floor(n/2). Direct prefix/suffix and height predicates agree at every primitive word. Independent C++17 enumeration matches the zero counts at n<16, 96 labeled words and precisely the six displayed necklaces at n=16. Both embedded checkers executed successfully; no infinite-domain conclusion is drawn from finite enumeration.

evidence: Charlier--Harju--Puzynina--Zamboni 2015, Proposition 2 gives a block-concatenation construction with every sufficiently long factor Abelian bordered and the explicit sixteen-bit block 0101001100110011.
Christodoulakis et al. 2014 abstract describes distribution of shortest Abelian borders of single binary words.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The infinite-word construction implies existence of one 16-letter rotationwise example, but no lower bound on the shortest such primitive word or complete list of all length-16 primitive necklaces. Single-word marginal border counts do not imply a joint all-rotations census. Only the sharp cutoff and complete classification are asserted as new.

evidence: Charlier et al. 2015 §5 Proposition 2 uses blocks 010100110011 and 0101001100110011, and shows all factors of length at least 15 in the relevant aperiodic concatenations have Abelian borders.
Holub and Müller 2015 concern ordinary borders and establish at least two ordinary unbordered conjugates for every primitive binary word.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The construction covers existence at n=16: by placing two copies of its sixteen-letter block consecutively in an allowed aperiodic concatenation, every cyclic rotation appears among those length-16 factors. The classification here is stricter in the needed sense: no primitive word works at n<16; precisely 6 necklaces (96 words) work at n=16. These statements are not implications of the inspected propositions. Ordinary unbordered roots do not contradict the Abelian condition.

originality.rationale: The 2015 source covers existence of a 16-letter example, which is not claimed new. It does not give the sharp nonexistence below 16 or exhaustive six-necklace classification. The 2014 single-word census papers and the 2015 ordinary-border classification do not entail the rotationwise count. Targeted searches found no covering earlier formula; an inaccessible full 2014 paper remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: The complete 2014 Christodoulakis--Christou--Crochemore--Iliopoulos paper could not be read; its abstract is noncovering but does not rule out a previously published six-class table.
A direct or disguised classification might be present in unindexed combinatorics literature; search failures cannot establish global novelty.
The length-16 existence construction is explicitly prior work and should not be advertised as newly discovered.

value.rationale: The first length at which a primitive word can lose all Abelian-unbordered conjugates is a natural sharp boundary contrasting the classical ordinary-border theorem. The complete list of six necklaces and balanced-only content is a meaningful finite structural classification, beyond the previously published example at n=16. It gives exact benchmarks for circular border detection, without requiring an unproved general larger-length statement.
